text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a sustained spike in log ingest from eu-west1 GPU hosts starting ~09:40 UTC. Loki disk usage climbed and we hit the ingest rate cap briefly. Seeing ~3x normal _lines_ingested_.

sunil: Thanks. Any correlation id or trace to root cause? quick grep?

maria: digging. Initial filter: `
{job=~"fluentd|node-exporter"} |= "gpu-device" | json | gpu_id
`
returns tons of pod-start logs from a new training job rollout. Correlation id looks like `trace=tr-9a2f` in the log payload.

jules: Is this the canary rollout for the large-model training? I pushed a change yesterday that increased init debug logging.

maria: yup that matches. Can we reduce verbosity before it burns us? We're seeing indexing spikes and hot shard warnings in Kibana.

devon: Quick mitigations: 1) Enable per-tenant sampling in Loki for eu-west1 fluentd streams. 2) Shorten index TTL for ingest-heavy indices from 30d -> 7d while we triage. 3) Alert threshold change so we don't get pager for transient bursts.

sunil: For sampling, use the `pipeline_stages` in fluentd to drop repetitive lines, or in Loki set `sampling` with `match_re` to keep 1/10 of repeats. Example snippet:```yaml
pipeline_stages:
  - regex: \"request_id=(?<req>[^ ]+)\"
  - drop: \"req =~ /debug/ and count(req) > 1\"
```
(rough)

jules: I can roll a patch to reduce debug logs in the training job. Will revert verbosity flag and redeploy canary.

maria: Meanwhile, Kibana query I ran to find affected indices: `index: logs-* AND message:\"trace=tr-9a2f\"` — shows heavy writes to `logs-2025.08.01` and `logs-2025.08.02`.

devon: On ILM, we should create a short-lived write alias for ingest spikes so rollover happens faster and we reclaim space. Also force merge older shards to reduce retention overhead. But force-merge is heavy. Prefer decreasing `index.lifecycle.rollover_alias` and `max_age`.

sunil: Agree. I'll change ILM for `logs-high-ingest-*` to 7d retention and lower `max_primary_shard_size` to 10gb for the hot tier, then monitor. Will run during low traffic window (in ~20m).

maria: Prometheus alerts that fired: `loki_ingestion_rate` spike and `es_index_pressure_hot_nodes`. Linked Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/logs-ingest?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now
We also saw a few GPU provisioning failures because the provisioning job waits on indexing confirmations — cascading.

jules: Noted. I'll pause the training canary for 30m. Pushing new image with reduced logs now.

devon: After ILM tweak, we should add a SLO dashboard that ties `lines_ingested` to cost per token and GPU queue latency. If ingestion spikes push legacy indexes, cost goes up. I can prototype a dashboard widget.

sunil: One more: add a temporary alert mute for `loki_ingestion_rate` for eu-west1 so ops noise is minimized while we stabilize (but keep the `es_index_pressure` pager).

maria: Actions: @jules pause canary + push reduced-logging image (in progress), @sunil ILM + mute alert (scheduled in 10m), @devon sampling rule + dashboard widget. I'll keep thread updates. :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: Incident annotation: ingest_rate_cap applied to tenant `training-canary` at 2025-08-01T09:45:12Z by policy `auto-throttle`.

maria: Update — jules paused canary, we've started seeing ingestion decline. Disk use trending down on node-05.

devon: Sampling rule applied to fluentd pipeline; reduced repeated pod init lines by ~88% in test. Dash widget draft: `lines_ingested / gpu_queue_latency`. Will post link soon.

sunil: ILM change applied to `logs-high-ingest-euwest-*`. Retention now 7d. Monitoring task started.

maria: Last: adding a short note in runbook to avoid heavy debug flags on training rollout and to run a simulated log spike test in staging before large canaries.

jules: +1, will add the runbook note. Thanks all. :rocket:
